- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true values by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than observed.
- Forecasts often peak too early and then drop too fast, missing the true “bottom” or “recovery” phase.
- Model underestimates low-price periods when true values dip below 80–82, especially after a high.
- Forecast sensitivity to recent history is too strong — model reacts too aggressively to short-term noise.
- Model fails to capture “recovery” phases after corrections — tends to stay flat or overcorrect.
